recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the Security work group wants stricter or differently located OAuth-profile wording, handle that as a fresh editorial/security-page tracker rather than as a missed application of FHIR-16534.
issue_request: FHIR-16534 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification for the Security work group. It asked the FHIR security checklist to add Authorization/Access Control guidance that when OAuth is used, an OAuth profile is needed, and that the SMART-on-FHIR App Authorization Guide should be considered where appropriate.
initial_application: Historical commit 95ee245e72e4bd1ac09824738ae7b5f7519239ef applied the issue as part of security narrative fixes, adding the OAuth-profile and SMART wording to source/security.html under the Authentication summary item while leaving the Authorization/Access Control summary focused on the FHIR Security Label infrastructure.
additional_context: FHIR-34362 later revisited the same security checklist and OAuth access-control wording, adding a separate When using OAuth checklist item for OAuth best-current-practice and adding token expiration/scope to access-control context. Subsequent security-page cleanup in FHIR-53717, FHIR-53923, and FHIR-56089 refined adjacent summary text and anchors without changing the OAuth/SMART substance. Current source/security.html recommends OAuth and HL7 SMART App Launch in the summary and access-control implementation section; source/secpriv-module.html recommends OAuth-based SMART for third-party app authorization; source/safety.html still calls for an appropriate OAuth profile, preferably SMART App Launch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Re-adding the exact older sentence would duplicate nearby active guidance and risk editorial drift without changing implementer understanding of the current specification.
